page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across most standard workloads, though raw computational throughput shows some limitations. The instance achieves average ratings in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, as well as in Passmark CPU encryption and database operations. However, stress-ng single-core performance falls into the bottom 10%, and multi-core stress-ng results are in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show average speeds for cached small-block reads but drop to the bottom 25% for uncached large-block reads and writes.

Given its high memory density relative to CPU resources, the ecs.r6a.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense, sustained CPU computation. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs positions this instance specifically for memory-intensive applications. It is well-suited for database operations, Redis caching layers, and general-purpose memory-heavy tasks, while being less optimal for CPU-bound physics simulations or high-throughput uncached memory operations.
